summary: Native Node addon harvests Chromium cookies and saved logins
details: The package ships a single ~10MB Linux x64 ELF Node N-API addon (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) with no JS wrapper, no source, and a stub README. The binary's readable strings contain the exact Chromium Cookies database schema fragments (host_key, top_frame_site_key, has_cross_site_ancestor, cookies_unique_index) and Chromium Login Data reader text ('Found login for'), together with an outbound HTTPS client stack (ureq/hyper/rustls) and proxy handling (HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY) — the shape of a browser cookie and saved-password stealer that reads the installer's user profile and can transmit it over TLS. The package name masquerades as a platform-native subpackage (linux-x64-gnu suffix) but has no parent package, and the version string '3.1.42-origin-chrom-468-delete-windows-32-bit-changelog-fix-410-1785839786' is noise consistent with dependency-confusion or typosquat delivery rather than a real release. Any consumer that require()s and invokes this addon on a developer or CI host exposes browser session cookies and stored credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
